data.narrative:
AstroForge is a Series A-stage space and aerospace company founded by Matt Gialich and Jose Acain that has raised approximately $56M to date. The private frontier-tech space sector includes 5 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 identifiable private peers spanning similar development stages and adjacent verticals, though direct same-stage peer data remains sparse.

Stage-progression analysis, the applicable triangulation method, uses the $56M total capital raised as a baseline and applies a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage step-ups, implying a $112M valuation. This method directly reflects the company's progress and capital intensity in its sector. Peer-median comparison was not viable; while 14 same-sector private companies exist, fewer than three qualified as precise same-stage or similar-tier comparables, making sector-wide medians unreliable. Public-comp anchoring via the 27.4x P/S median across Space & Aerospace public names cannot be applied due to absence of AstroForge's disclosed revenue.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $95M (low) to $129M (high), with $112M as the central point. This single-method derivation carries material uncertainty. Key sensitivities include actual operational milestones achieved since the last funding round and trajectory to Series B financing conditions. The sparse comparable set for Series A space-tech companies limits cross-validation; revenue disclosure or additional private funding data would materially improve precision.
